title: Fermi shares surge on AMD credit support deal for Texas AI site
source_used: Investing.com report, read in the Yahoo Finance copy
key_facts: Fermi Inc (NASDAQ: FRMI) shares jumped 13.2% in premarket trading on Tuesday 13 Oct 2026 after announcing a credit support agreement with AMD for Project Matador in Carson County, Texas.
The agreement supports a lease for phase one of the project, which will deliver 222 megawatts of gross power capacity, and is a key milestone toward project financing.
The companies also signed a framework agreement for potential expansion of up to 650 MW of gross power capacity.
The credit support agreement relates to Fermi's first customer lease, announced 10 Aug 2026; the article does not name the lessee.
Fermi has invested more than $1.5 billion in the buildout to date; the project provides power infrastructure for AI computing facilities, behind the meter on a private grid.
Subject to binding customer agreements, the project is expected to scale to approximately 17 GW.
Lee McIntire, Fermi's chief executive, and Mathew Hein, AMD's senior vice president and chief strategy officer of corporate development, are quoted welcoming the partnership.
quote_evidence: Investing.com -- Fermi Inc (NASDAQ:FRMI) shares jumped 13.2% in premarket trading Tuesday after the company announced a credit support agreement with AMD for its Project Matador AI infrastructure development in Carson County, Texas.
The agreement with Advanced Micro Devices Inc (NASDAQ:AMD) supports a lease for phase one of the project, which will deliver 222 megawatts of gross power capacity.
Subject to entering into binding customer agreements, the project is expected to scale to approximately 17 GW, with capital deployment matched to commercial commitments.
why_it_matters_hint: A chip maker backing the first lease is a step toward financing a very large AI power and computing site.
notes: Investing.com wrote the report; it was read on Yahoo Finance, which carries it, so the Investing.com page was not opened and the link is the Yahoo copy. The article does not say who the lessee is and does not say what form AMD's credit support takes, beyond backing the lease.
